title: Why Doesn't Your Screen Work With Gloves? 🧤
description: Your phone screen senses the electricity in your body! Discover the invisible grid of wires under the glass — and why gloves don't work.

scenes.say: Try touching your phone with gloves on. Nothing happens! But your bare finger works instantly. Why?

scenes.caption: A grid of clear wires
scenes.say: Under the glass is a grid of almost invisible wires, holding a tiny electric charge all the time.
Your body conducts electricity. When you touch the screen, you draw away a little charge at that spot, and the chip knows exactly where your finger is.

scenes.label: The screen scans for touch
scenes.say: The screen scans the whole grid more than a hundred and twenty times a second, which is why it tracks your finger so smoothly.

scenes.text: Anything conductive can work the screen
scenes.say: Fun fact: anything that conducts electricity works on the screen, even a sausage! Gloves are insulators, so the charge can't flow.

scenes.text: Next: How does Wi-Fi reach you?
scenes.say: Subscribe to How It Works. Next time: how does the internet reach your phone with no wires at all?
